description: Senior engineer level (5 to 8 years professional experience). Evaluates distributed system architecture at scale, fault tolerance, operational excellence, risk mitigation, developer velocity, technical mentorship, and driving consensus across teams.

axes.depth: Mastery of distributed consensus, CAP/PACELC trade-offs, network partitions, multi-region replication, observability, and cost-performance boundaries.
axes.ambiguity: High ambiguity; prompts often present ill-defined business problems where the candidate must define scope, constraints, and success metrics.
axes.expectedScope: Multi-system or cross-service domain, core platform components, long-term tech debt strategy, and company-wide standards.
axes.followUpPressure: Deep stress-testing on extreme traffic spikes, cascade failures, data corruption recovery, blast radius containment, and cost efficiency.
axes.behavioralExpectations: Exemplary technical leadership, navigating cross-team politics constructively, fostering psychological safety, and driving blameless post-mortems.

relevance.name: Relevance & Directness
relevance.description: Grounds high-level architecture in organizational constraints, team topology, ROI, and reliability goals.

anchors.1: Over-engineers needlessly, introducing trendy technologies without considering maintenance burden, team skills, or cost.
anchors.3: Focuses on pragmatic architecture; balances scalability needs against delivery timelines, maintenance cost, and complexity.
anchors.5: Strategically precise: frames architecture around business outcomes, risk boundaries, organizational bandwidth, and evolutionary design.

structure.name: Structural Framing
structure.description: Flawlessly frames complex distributed architectures from executive summary to deep technical failure analysis.

anchors.1: Scattered coverage that fails to define boundaries, data models, or SLAs before jumping into specific tooling.
anchors.3: Methodical framework: defines SLAs/SLOs, maps component topologies, evaluates data flow, and establishes failure domains.
anchors.5: Executive-grade delivery: structures complex multi-system solutions into clear milestones, risk registers, and architectural principles.

depth.name: Technical & Conceptual Depth
depth.description: Deep distributed systems expertise: replication topologies, consensus protocols, split-brain handling, and backpressure.

anchors.1: Superficial hand-waving on critical topics like data consistency, idempotency keys, partition tolerance, or graceful degradation.
anchors.3: Deep technical grasp: details Raft/Paxos implications, event-driven architectures, circuit breakers, and database sharding.
anchors.5: Authoritative mastery: analyzes tail-latency amplification, distributed transaction trade-offs (2PC vs Saga), and disaster recovery runbooks.

clarity.name: Clarity & Articulation
clarity.description: Communicates with high emotional intelligence, commanding executive presence, and crisp precision.

anchors.1: Combative or excessively dogmatic delivery; defensive when questioned or unable to articulate alternative points of view.
anchors.3: Clear, persuasive, and open-minded communication; welcomes pushback and defends decisions with objective data.
anchors.5: Inspiring, crystal-clear delivery; translates complex technical nuances into accessible analogies while maintaining rigorous precision.

levelFit.name: Level Alignment
levelFit.description: Calibrated against senior engineer expectations of technical leadership, blast-radius containment, and strategic foresight.

anchors.1: Operates as a mid-level task executor who lacks systemic foresight, risk awareness, or cross-team leadership.
anchors.3: Strong senior engineer: leads architectural design, anticipates operational hurdles, and elevates team members.
anchors.5: Operates at staff caliber: connects low-level system details to multi-quarter business strategy and organizational capability.
